mainTopic: Sources for a full sister and for the מפטם and סך of שמן המשחה, and the source of the warning against a טמא eating קודש
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question. רבי יצחק learns that a sister who is the daughter of both his father and his mother is forbidden from the first אחותו in ויקרא כ:יז. רבנן use that word instead to teach that one who blends (מפטם) and one who smears (סך) שמן המשחה are each liable on their own. For רבי יצחק, the גמרא gives two possible sources for that rule: רבי אלעזר's general rule that two לאוין with one כרת are separate for a קרבן, or the verse about אשה דוה. רבנן need that verse for the rule that a woman is a נדה only when the blood comes out through her ערוה. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's case of a טמא who eats קודש and asks where the תורה writes the warning (אזהרה) against it. ריש לקיש says it comes from 'בכל קדש לא תגע'. רבי יוחנן learns it from a גזירה שוה of 'טומאתו'. The גמרא defends ריש לקיש against two challenges, and a ברייתא supports him by comparing קודש to מקדש. The amud ends with a new rule from רבי יוחנן: a לאו that has an עשה before it brings מלקות.

steps.title: רבי יצחק learns the case of a sister from both parents from 'his sister' at the start of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes answering where רבי יצחק learns that one is liable for a sister who is the daughter of both his father and his mother: from the word אחותו at the beginning of the verse in ויקרא כ:יז.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the word 'his sister' at the beginning of the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question asked just before this amud: where does רבי יצחק learn that a sister who is both his father's and his mother's daughter is forbidden? Answer: from the word אחותו at the start of the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about a sister mentions אחותו twice, once at the start and once at the end. The verse could have said only 'his father's daughter or his mother's daughter' without the first אחותו. So רבי יצחק uses that first word to include a sister who is the daughter of both parents.

keyTerms.meaning: His sister; the word in the verse (ויקרא כ:יז) being used as a source
Of the beginning; here, the first time the word appears in the verse
A sister who is the daughter of both his father and his mother

phrases.english: From 'his sister' at the beginning [of the verse].
phrases.notes: This finishes an answer from the last amud. The פסוק is ויקרא כ:יז, which says אחותו at its start and end; the first one covers a sister from both parents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the earlier question of where רבי יצחק learns liability for a sister who is the daughter of both parents.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יצחק learns liability for a sister from both parents from the first mention of אחותו in the verse.

steps.title: רבנן need that word for the מפטם and the סך of שמן המשחה
steps.stepSummary: רבנן do not need the first אחותו for anything about a sister, so they use that word to teach that the מפטם and the סך of שמן המשחה are each liable separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side, רבנן: they need that word to separate the כרת, giving one for the one who blends the oil and one for the one who smears it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבנן do with the first אחותו. They use it for an unrelated lesson about שמן המשחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in שמות ל:לג lists two acts, blending the oil (מפטם) and putting it on someone (סך), but writes only one כרת. Since רבנן learn nothing about a sister from the first אחותו, they use it to teach that each act is its own sin, with its own כרת or its own חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one; the other opinion in the argument
He needs it (for a different lesson)
One who blends a copy of שמן המשחה
One who smears שמן המשחה on someone not allowed to use it
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven for certain sins done on purpose

phrases.english: And the other: that one is needed by him,
phrases.notes: 'The other' here is רבנן, and 'that one' is the first אחותו.

phrases.english: to divide the karet for the one who blends and for the one who smears.
phrases.notes: The פסוק is שמות ל:לג, about the holy anointing oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question: what do רבנן learn from the first אחותו, if not the law of a sister from both parents?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן use the first אחותו to separate the liability of the מפטם and the סך.

steps.title: רבי יצחק follows רבי אלעזר's rule: two לאוין with one כרת are separate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יצחק knows the מפטם and סך are separate. Answer: he holds like רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי הושעיא, that two לאוין with one כרת are always separate for קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other, רבי יצחק, where does he learn it? He holds like what רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי הושעיא. רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי הושעיא: Any place where you find two prohibitions and only one כרת, they are separate for bringing a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: if רבי יצחק used the first אחותו for a sister from both parents, how does he know the מפטם and סך are separate? It answers with a general rule from רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יצחק there is no need for a special word. There is a general rule: when the תורה gives two separate לאוין but only one כרת, each one still counts on its own for a חטאת. Since the מפטם and the סך are two separate לאוין, they are separate automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: Negative commandments, 'do not' prohibitions
They are separate for a קרבן: each one, done by mistake, needs its own חטאת
An offering; here a חטאת brought for a sin done by mistake

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's rule: two לאוין with one כרת are each counted separately for a קרבן.

phrases.english: And the other?
phrases.notes: Now 'the other' is רבי יצחק: how does he know the blender and the smearer are separate?

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא,
phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Hoshaya:
Any place where you find
two prohibitions and one karet,
they are separate with regard to an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? סָבַר כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to רבי יצחק and asks how he covers the lesson that רבנן learned from the first אחותו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does רבי יצחק know the מפטם and סך are liable separately?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He uses the general rule of רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי הושעיא: two לאוין with one כרת are separate for a קרבן.

steps.title: Second answer: רבי יצחק learns it from the verse about a woman who is a נדה
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: רבי יצחק does not hold like רבי אלעזר, and he learns that the מפטם and סך are separate from the verse 'וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכַּב אֶת אִשָּׁה דָּוָה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: he does not hold like רבי אלעזר, and he learns it from the verse 'And a man who lies with a woman who is unwell (a נדה).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to explain רבי יצחק. Instead of the general rule, he uses a different extra verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe רבי יצחק does not accept רבי אלעזר's rule at all. Then he needs a source, and he finds it in the verse about a נדה in ויקרא כ:יח. That verse is not needed for its own topic, so it can teach the lesson about the מפטם and the סך.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say; introduces a second, different answer
He derives it, he learns it from
Unwell; in this verse, a woman who is a נדה

steps.confusionAlert: The verse about a נדה is not teaching anything new about נדה here. It is used as an extra verse to teach the separate rule about the מפטם and the סך of שמן המשחה.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers for רבי יצחק: either the general rule of רבי אלעזר, or the extra verse about אשה דוה.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
he does not hold like Rabbi Elazar,
and he derives it

phrases.aramaic: מִ״וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכַּב אֶת אִשָּׁה דָּוָה״.
phrases.english: from 'And a man who lies with a woman who is unwell.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:18.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation for רבי יצחק instead of relying on רבי אלעזר's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יצחק must depend on רבי אלעזר's general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even without that rule, רבי יצחק has a source: the extra verse about אשה דוה.

steps.title: What do the other opinion learn from this verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבנן do with the verse of אשה דוה, since they do not use it the way רבי יצחק does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion, what do they do with that verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about רבנן. If they do not use 'ואיש אשר ישכב את אשה דוה' for the מפטם and סך, what do they learn from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, רבי יצחק used this verse to teach that the מפטם and סך are separate. Every word in the תורה must teach something. So the other side, רבנן, must use the verse for some other lesson, and the גמרא wants to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the other opinion

phrases.english: And the other [opinion]?
phrases.notes: He means רבנן: what do they learn from the verse of אשה דוה that רבי יצחק just used?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing opinion uses the verse that step 4 gave to רבי יצחק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבנן learn from 'ואיש אשר ישכב את אשה דוה'.

steps.title: The verse teaches that a woman is טמאה only when blood leaves through her ערוה
steps.stepSummary: רבנן need the verse for רבי יוחנן's teaching in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: a woman is a נדה only if the blood comes out through her ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is needed for רבי יוחנן's teaching. רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: How do we know that a woman is not טמאה unless her blood comes out through her ערוה? Because it says, 'And a man who lies with a woman who is דוה and uncovers her ערוה.' This teaches that she is not טמאה unless her blood comes out through her ערוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבנן use the verse for a different lesson. It teaches that a woman becomes טמאה as a נדה only when the blood comes out through her ערוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse puts 'דוה' (the bleeding woman) next to 'וגלה את ערותה' (uncovers her ערוה). From this we learn that the bleeding has to come from that place. Blood from anywhere else does not make her a נדה. Since רבנן use the verse for this, it is not free to teach about the מפטם and סך.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is bleeding, meaning a נדה
Her menstrual blood
Her ערוה (private area)
This teaches

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק uses 'אשה דוה' to teach that the מפטם and סך are separate. רבנן use it for רבי יוחנן's teaching that נדה blood must come through the ערוה.

phrases.english: That [verse] is needed by him for that of Rabbi Yoḥanan,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
From where do we know that a woman is not impure
unless her menstrual blood comes out through her private area?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכַּב אֶת אִשָּׁה דָּוָה
phrases.english: As it is said: “And a man who lies with a woman who is afflicted”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:18

phrases.english: “and uncovers her nakedness, etc.”
This teaches that a woman is not impure
unless her menstrual blood comes out through her private area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by giving רבנן their own lesson from the verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן use the verse for the teaching that נדה blood must come out through the ערוה to make a woman טמאה.

steps.title: For a טמא who enters the מקדש, both punishment and warning are written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's case of a טמא who ate קודש. First it says that a טמא entering the מקדש is easy to explain, since the תורה writes both a punishment and a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'a טמא who ate קודש' gets מלקות. It makes sense for one who comes into the מקדש while טמא, because both a punishment and a warning are written. The punishment: 'He made the משכן of ה׳ טמא, and he will be cut off.' The warning: 'And they shall not make their camp טמא.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic from the משנה. Here it is setting up the next question by showing a case where everything is clearly written in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To get מלקות, there has to be a written לאו (a warning). A כרת punishment by itself is not enough. For a טמא who enters the מקדש, the תורה gives both a כרת and a לאו. This sets up the contrast in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for this case (sets up a contrast with an 'אֶלָּא' case)
The punishment written in the תורה (here, כרת)
A warning, meaning a written לאו that forbids the act
One who enters the מקדש while טמא

steps.confusionAlert: עונש and אזהרה are two different things. The עונש (כרת) tells us the punishment, but we also need a written אזהרה (a לאו) before we can say the act is forbidden and give מלקות.

phrases.english: “And an impure person who ate sacrificial food.”
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה's list of people who get מלקות.

phrases.english: Granted, one who enters the Temple impure –
a punishment is written and a warning is written:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹנֶשׁ – דִּכְתִיב: ״אֶת מִשְׁכַּן ה׳ טִמֵּא וְנִכְרְתָה״.
phrases.english: Punishment – as it is written: “He has made impure the Tabernacle of God, and he shall be cut off.”
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:13

phrases.english: Warning – “And they shall not make their camp impure.”
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה, moving away from the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא who enters the מקדש has both a written עונש (כרת) and a written אזהרה (לאו).

steps.title: Where is the warning for a טמא who eats קודש?
steps.stepSummary: For a טמא who eats קודש, the כרת punishment is written, but the גמרא asks where the warning (לאו) is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for a טמא who ate קודש, the punishment is written: 'And the person who eats meat from the שלמים of ה׳ while his טומאה is on him will be cut off.' But where is the warning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks its real question. Where does the תורה write a לאו against a טמא eating קודש, so that he can get מלקות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the מקדש case, here we only see the כרת. Without a written warning there should be no מלקות. Yet the משנה says he gets מלקות, so there must be a source for the warning.

keyTerms.meaning: A peace offering (שלמים)
And he will be cut off, meaning כרת
Where is the warning learned from?

phrases.english: But an impure person who ate sacrificial food,
granted, a punishment is written –

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכַל בָּשָׂר מִזֶּבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים אֲשֶׁר לַה׳
phrases.english: “And the soul that eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to God”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:20

phrases.english: “while his impurity is upon him, shall be cut off,”
but from where is the warning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the eating case with the מקדש case from step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the לאו (warning) against a טמא eating קודש.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the warning is 'בכל קדש לא תגע'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the warning comes from 'בכל קדש לא תגע' ('she shall not touch any קודש').
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: 'She shall not touch any קודש.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers with a פסוק that forbids a טמא from touching קודש. He uses this as the warning against eating it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is said about a woman after birth who is still טמאה. ריש לקיש reads it as the source of the לאו for any טמא eating קודש. This gives the משנה the written warning it needs for מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: She shall not touch any holy thing

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says:
“She shall not touch any consecrated item.”
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:4, said about a woman after giving birth who is still טמאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אזהרה is 'בכל קדש לא תגע'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a גזירה שוה from 'טומאתו' and 'טומאתו'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes ברדלא. The word 'טומאתו' appears in both the eating case and the מקדש case, so the eating case gets both a punishment and a warning, just like the מקדש case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says that ברדלא taught: We learn 'טומאתו' from 'טומאתו'. Here it is written, 'and his טומאה is on him, and he will be cut off.' There it is written, 'he will be טמא, his טומאה is still on him.' Just as there, there is a punishment and a warning, so too here there is a punishment and a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. He uses a גזירה שוה to take the warning from the מקדש case and apply it to the eating case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'טומאתו' appears in the eating פסוק and in the מקדש פסוק. Because of this shared word, the two cases are linked. The מקדש case has both עונש and אזהרה (step 7), so the eating case also has an אזהרה, and that is why he gets מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes, meaning it is learned through a גזירה שוה
His טומאה, the shared word that links the two פסוקים
Just as there, so too here (the formula of a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for the warning against a טמא eating קודש. ריש לקיש uses 'בכל קדש לא תגע'. רבי יוחנן (from ברדלא) uses a גזירה שוה of 'טומאתו' to compare it to entering the מקדש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says that Bardela taught:
It is derived from “his impurity” and “his impurity,”
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word in two places links the two laws together.

phrases.english: it is written here: “and his impurity is upon him, and he shall be cut off,”

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב הָתָם ״טָמֵא יִהְיֶה עוֹד טֻמְאָתוֹ בּוֹ״,
phrases.english: and it is written there: “he shall be impure, his impurity is still upon him,”
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:13, the פסוק about a טמא who enters the מקדש.

phrases.english: just as there, there is punishment and warning –
so too here, there is punishment and warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different source for the warning, in place of ריש לקיש's פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'טומאתו' carries the אזהרה from entering the מקדש over to eating קודש.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יוחנן use ריש לקיש's verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why ריש לקיש rejects רבי יוחנן's source, but asks why רבי יוחנן rejects ריש לקיש's simpler source.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that ריש לקיש didn't learn like רבי יוחנן, because he never received that גזירה שוה from his teachers. But why didn't רבי יוחנן learn like ריש לקיש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two answers from steps 9 and 10. It asks what reason רבי יוחנן has for not using the clear פסוק that ריש לקיש quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may only use a גזירה שוה if he received it from his teachers, so ריש לקיש's position is easy to explain. ריש לקיש's verse, 'בכל קדש לא תגע', looks like a direct warning. So the גמרא needs to know why רבי יוחנן went looking for a גזירה שוה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (one side is understood, the other is not)
Learning one case from another because the same word appears in both; it must be received from one's teachers
He did not learn it (did not receive it as a tradition)
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא, רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן –
phrases.english: It makes sense that Reish Lakish did not say like Rabbi Yochanan –

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: that verse is a warning about תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that 'בכל קדש לא תגע' is a warning about תרומה, not קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: that verse is a warning about תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן. He reads the word 'קודש' in that פסוק as referring to תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not deny that the פסוק gives a warning. He holds the warning is about תרומה, a lower level of holiness. That leaves no פסוק for קדשים, so he needs the גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Where does ריש לקיש get the warning for תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: If ריש לקיש uses 'בכל קדש לא תגע' for קדשים, the גמרא asks where he finds the warning for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש, where does he learn the warning about תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to ריש לקיש. Since he used the verse for קדשים, it asks what his source is for the תרומה warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that a טמא may not eat תרומה. So ריש לקיש also needs a source for that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he learn it?

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, אַזְהָרָה לִתְרוּמָה מְנָא לֵיהּ?

steps.title: ריש לקיש learns תרומה from 'איש איש מזרע אהרן'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns the תרומה warning from the פסוק about a צרוע or זב of זרע אהרן. The only food equally shared by all of אהרן's descendants is תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'Any man of the descendants of אהרן who is a צרוע or a זב'. Which item is the same for all of אהרן's descendants? You must say it is תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives ריש לקיש a different פסוק for תרומה. That frees 'בכל קדש לא תגע' for קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'זרע אהרן' point to something every descendant of אהרן may eat, men and women alike. Some קדשים may only be eaten by male כהנים, but תרומה is eaten by all. So this פסוק must be about תרומה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: one verse is for eating, the other for touching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן does with the 'זרע אהרן' verse. He uses it for eating תרומה, and 'בכל קדש לא תגע' for touching תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי יוחנן)? That verse is for eating, and this one is for touching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks briefly why רבי יוחנן needs two פסוקים for תרומה, and answers right away. Each פסוק teaches a different action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is: if 'זרע אהרן' already warns about תרומה, why does רבי יוחנן also need 'בכל קדש לא תגע' for תרומה? The answer splits them. 'זרע אהרן' forbids a טמא from eating תרומה, and 'לא תגע' forbids a טמא from touching it.

steps.title: ריש לקיש already needs that verse for touching קודש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש: 'בכל קדש לא תגע' is needed for a טמא who touches קודש, so how can it also be the warning for eating?
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש, does 'בכל קדש לא תגע' really come for this? He needs it for a טמא who touched קודש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's source from step 9. It says he already uses this פסוק for a different rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק literally says 'touch'. If ריש לקיש uses it to punish a טמא who touches קודש, it seems used up. Then it cannot also be the warning for eating קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it come for this purpose?

Holy food, here meaning קדשים (sacrificial food)

steps.title: Proof: the dispute about a טמא who touched קודש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that ריש לקיש uses the פסוק for touching. He holds that a טמא who touched קודש gets מלקות because of 'בכל קדש לא תגע', while רבי יוחנן uses it for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: a טמא who touched קודש. ריש לקיש says he gets מלקות; רבי יוחנן says he does not. ריש לקיש says he gets מלקות because of 'בכל קדש לא תגע'. רבי יוחנן says he does not, because that פסוק comes as a warning about תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a known מחלוקת to back up its challenge. It shows that ריש לקיש really does use this פסוק for touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms the problem from step 16. ריש לקיש gives מלקות for touching based on this exact פסוק. רבי יוחנן gives no מלקות for touching קדשים, since for him the פסוק is about תרומה.

steps.title: One verse, two lessons: touching from the word, eating from the הקש
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns both rules from the one פסוק. The word 'touch' teaches the touching rule. The eating warning comes because קודש is placed next to מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טמא who touched קודש: since the תורה used the language of touching, we learn that rule from it. The warning for one who eats: קודש is linked to מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge for ריש לקיש. The single פסוק carries two separate lessons, each from a different feature of the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The touching rule comes from the plain word 'תגע'. The eating warning comes from a הקש: the same פסוק continues with the מקדש, so קודש and מקדש are linked. Just as entering the מקדש has a warning, eating קודש does too. So the פסוק is not used up.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the תורה‎ / ה׳)
The wording of 'touching'
Is compared through a הקש (two things placed side by side in a פסוק are linked)
The בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש: 'בכל קדש לא תגע' teaches both touching (from its wording) and eating (from the הקש of קודש to מקדש). רבי יוחנן: the פסוק is about תרומה, and the warning for eating קדשים comes from the גזירה שוה of 'טומאתו'.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think ריש לקיש learns eating from the word 'touch'. The word 'touch' only teaches touching. Eating comes from the side-by-side placement of קודש and מקדש.

steps.terutzMaskana: The wording teaches touching, and the הקש of קודש to מקדש teaches the eating warning, so ריש לקיש's source stands

steps.title: Isn't that פסוק needed for eating before the blood is sprinkled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש again: 'בכל קדש לא תגע' is already used for a טמא who eats קודש before זריקת דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, does that verse come to teach this? ריש לקיש needs it for an impure person who ate sacrificial meat before the blood was sprinkled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem for ריש לקיש. The פסוק he uses for the eating warning is already busy teaching a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18, ריש לקיש got both touching and eating from 'בכל קדש לא תגע'. Now the גמרא says he uses this פסוק for a third rule as well: a טמא who eats קודש before זריקת דמים. Can one פסוק carry all of that?

keyTerms.meaning: And still, there is another problem
He needs it for something else
Meat of a קרבן
Sprinkling the קרבן's blood on the מזבח, which normally makes the meat allowed to eat

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is already used for eating before זריקה, so it seems it cannot also serve as the general eating warning.

steps.title: The מחלוקת about eating before זריקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the מחלוקת: ריש לקיש says a טמא who eats קודש before זריקה gets מלקות, and רבי יוחנן says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: an impure person who ate sacrificial meat before the blood was sprinkled. ריש לקיש says he is flogged, and רבי יוחנן says he is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge by quoting a known argument. It shows that ריש לקיש really does hold there is מלקות before זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proves the claim made in step 19. Since ריש לקיש gives מלקות even before זריקה, he must have a פסוק for it, and that פסוק will turn out to be 'בכל קדש'.

keyTerms.meaning: He gets מלקות (lashes)
He does not get מלקות

steps.title: The reasons behind each side
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns מלקות from 'בכל קדש לא תגע', which makes no difference between before and after זריקה. רבי יוחנן's source, 'טומאתו טומאתו', is written about after זריקה, so there is no מלקות before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says he is flogged because of 'No holy thing shall she touch', which makes no difference between before sprinkling and after sprinkling. רבי יוחנן says he is not flogged. רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, since he learns it from 'his impurity' and 'his impurity', and where 'his impurity' is written, it is talking about after the sprinkling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each אמורא holds what he does. This sharpens the question against ריש לקיש, which the next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, 'בכל קדש' is general, so it covers before and after זריקה alike. רבי יוחנן learns the eating warning from the link between the two times the word 'טומאתו' appears, and the eating פסוק is about meat after זריקה. So before זריקה there is no לאו and no מלקות.

'His impurity', the word that links the eating פסוק to the מקדש פסוק

'No holy thing shall she touch',

steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: מלקות before זריקה, from 'בכל קדש'. רבי יוחנן: no מלקות, since 'טומאתו' is written about after זריקה.

steps.title: Before-זריקה comes from the word 'בכל'
steps.stepSummary: The answer for ריש לקיש: the before-זריקה case comes from the extra word 'בכל', so the rest of the פסוק is free for touching and eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: That case is learned from 'בכל קדש', 'any holy thing'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 19. ריש לקיש gets the before-זריקה rule from the word 'בכל' ('any').
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בכל' is an including word: 'any' holy thing, even meat before זריקה. Since that rule hangs on the extra word, the פסוק itself can still teach touching and, through its closeness to מקדש, eating.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Any', an including word that widens the rule
It is learned from
That case (eating before זריקה)

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש gets three things from 'בכל קדש לא תגע': touching (the word 'תגע'), eating (it sits next to 'מקדש'), and eating before זריקה (the word 'בכל').

phrases.english: That is derived from 'any holy thing'.
phrases.notes: The extra word 'בכל' ('any') reaches even meat whose blood has not yet been sprinkled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different words of the same פסוק teach different laws
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole פסוק is used up by the before-זריקה case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the word 'בכל' teaches before-זריקה, so the rest of the פסוק remains for touching and eating.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'בכל קדש לא תגע' as a warning against eating, just like ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in line with ריש לקיש: 'No holy thing shall she touch' is a warning for one who eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with ריש לקיש. The ברייתא says the touching פסוק is really a warning about eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is support from a תנאי source. רבי יוחנן learned the eating warning from the גזירה שוה of 'טומאתו', but this ברייתא matches ריש לקיש's reading of 'בכל קדש לא תגע'.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah warning, the לאו needed for punishment
One who eats

phrases.english: It was taught in line with Reish Lakish:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending ריש לקיש, the גמרא brings positive support for him.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that 'בכל קדש לא תגע' warns against eating

steps.title: Maybe it means touching?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the פסוק might just warn against touching, as its plain words say.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it is a warning for one who eats, or is it only a warning for one who touches?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks itself a question that sets up its proof. Since the פסוק says 'touch', maybe it is only about touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the obvious objection, because the plain word is 'תגע'. The ברייתא raises it so it can prove the eating reading in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who touches
Or perhaps it is only

phrases.english: Do you say it is a warning for one who eats,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר אַזְהָרָה לָאוֹכֵל, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא אַזְהָרָה לַנּוֹגֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא questions its own statement in order to prove it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the פסוק warn about eating or only about touching?

steps.title: Compared to מקדש, so it means eating
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק places קודש next to מקדש. Entering the מקדש while טמא brings a death-type punishment, so the קודש warning must also be for something with that punishment, which is eating and not touching.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'No holy thing shall she touch, and to the Temple...' It compares holy things to the Temple. Just as the Temple involves a matter punished by taking of life, so too every matter here involves taking of life. And if it meant touching, is there taking of life for that? Rather, it means eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves the eating reading by comparing קודש to מקדש in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא who enters the מקדש gets כרת, a punishment that takes a life. The הקש says the קודש warning must carry the same kind of punishment. Touching קודש has no such punishment, but eating it while טמא does, so the warning is about eating.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
It compares (a הֶקֵּשׁ, linking two things placed side by side)
Taking of a life, meaning כָּרֵת
Touching

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא learns the eating warning from the הקש of קודש to מקדש: both carry כרת, and touching does not.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't be thrown by the word 'touch' in the פסוק. The ברייתא uses the הקש to show the warning is about eating.

phrases.english: The verse states:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל קֹדֶשׁ לֹא תִגָּע וְאֶל הַמִּקְדָּשׁ וְגוֹ׳״ –
phrases.english: 'No holy thing shall she touch, and to the Temple...'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:4. The פסוק ends 'she shall not come'.

phrases.english: it compares holy things to the Temple:

phrases.aramaic: מָה מִקְדָּשׁ דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נְטִילַת נְשָׁמָה –
phrases.english: just as the Temple is a matter involving taking of life,
phrases.notes: Entering the מקדש while טמא is punished with כרת.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נְטִילַת נְשָׁמָה.
phrases.english: so too every matter involving taking of life.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בִּנְגִיעָה – מִי אִיכָּא נְטִילַת נְשָׁמָה?
phrases.english: And if it is about touching, is there taking of life?
Rather, it is about eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: בְּכׇל קֹדֶשׁ לֹא תִגָּע וְאֶל הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's own question from step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a warning for eating, proven by the הקש to מקדש and its כרת punishment.

steps.title: A לאו with an עשה before it brings מלקות
steps.stepSummary: A new rule from רבי יוחנן: any לא תעשה that comes after an עשה is punished with מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: for any negative commandment that a positive commandment came before, one is flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a rule from רבי יוחנן about which לאוין bring מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עשה that comes before the לאו does not stop the מלקות. Such a לאו is not treated like one that is fixed by doing an עשה afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment (לאו)
A positive commandment
That came before it
They are flogged

steps.whyThisMatters: Normally a לאו connected to an עשה may not bring מלקות. This rule says that when the עשה comes first, the מלקות stays.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
any negative commandment that a positive commandment preceded,
one is flogged for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁקְּדָמוֹ עֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the טמא who eats קודש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לא תעשה preceded by an עשה brings מלקות.
